items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: And then I listened to Jelly Roll Morton’s original “Jelly Roll Blues” and I got hooked on jazz.

ctx.x: No Doc. That’s not quite complete. You’ve seen the music business from a number of sides as a performer yourself, and now as managing and getting in to the logistics of moving around the world in music. Was there a time in your youth when you said I really want to be in music? At what point did you think that that might be possibility?

Do you know I don’t think I ever planned my life to begin with. I wish I could say that I had made big plans. But what happened to me was I was a kid growing up in the north of England, and of course jazz is not indigenous to the north of England. And I heard a recording of Bessie Smith. And all I can say, Monk, is that I didn’t understand. If you remember on that “Back Water Blues” and she sings “when it rains five days/and the sky turns black as night” I didn’t even know, really, what she said. When it rains…
You anticipated my next question. Were you kind of a club of one?
